clue.text: One with a suit may give tip to Ernie

indicators.note: these words say the letters of the following words may yield something else once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in a suit might hand Ernie a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may give' signals that TIP TO ERNIE is reshuffled; 'suit' reads as clothing but is a legal action or plea.
explanation.definitionFit: A petitioner presses a suit, in the old sense of a formal plea or lawsuit.

clue.text: One sings his praises

parts.note: read as someone praising a person, but 'his praises' are praise songs to God, the psalms of the Bible

explanation.definitionFit: The writer of the psalms, traditionally King David, composed hymns of praise to be sung.

clue.text: Kept a record that's scratched

definitions.meaning: to keep the tally of points in a game is to keep score
something gouged with lines has been marked with grooves

explanation.surface: A vinyl record that has been kept is now scratched.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is both to tally points and to cut lines into a surface, so the past tense fits each.

clue.text: Musicians forbidden to speak

indicators.note: these words ask for the word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: forbidden means banned

explanation.surface: Performers have been barred from talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Right-handed key

parts.note: reads like a key turned with the right hand, but the key is musical: at the piano the upper stave, played by the right hand, carries this sign

explanation.definitionFit: In piano music the right hand usually plays the stave marked with the G sign that fixes its pitch.

clue.text: Superior tram?

parts.note: read as an instruction, a word for market (MART) written upwards gives the clue word tram

explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' reverses: MART, a market, turned upwards spells TRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods are expensive and of superior quality.

clue.text: A coin's tossed in a gambling situation

indicators.note: tossed suggests the letters are thrown about like a flipped coin

parts.note: read here as the plural coins

explanation.surface: A coin is flipped at a betting venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino is a building where people gamble.

clue.text: Beat in a round of golf

indicators.note: to go round is to turn about, so the word golf is read the other way

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes an opponent during eighteen holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round of' turns GOLF backwards; 'a round of golf' looks like a game, not an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to beat with a whip or stick.

clue.text: Comfortable situation for a professor

parts.note: a professor holds a chair, a post; one that is undemanding would be a soft one, which is also a padded armchair

explanation.definitionFit: A padded armchair is a comfortable seat, while a professor's post is called a chair.

clue.text: A gem looks right in the ring

indicators.note: one letter sits inside the word for the ring

parts.note: a peal is the ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A jewel looks just right set in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks' is a link; 'ring' suggests jewellery but is the sound of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a gem formed inside an oyster.

clue.text: Denied a civil education

parts.note: reads as being refused civic schooling, but means never taught good manners in upbringing

explanation.definitionFit: Someone badly brought up lacks courtesy, never having been taught to be civil.

clue.text: Direction for making a machine part

definitions.meaning: a compass heading measured in degrees
a component that supports a rotating shaft, such as a ball race

explanation.surface: Instructions for building a part for a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing means a compass heading and also a component that lets a shaft rotate smoothly.

clue.text: Work I mislaid

indicators.note: the prefix mis- means wrongly, so the letters after it are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: I have lost my piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'mislaid' is split: 'mis' (wrongly) rearranges LAID, which follows I.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem is a famous literary work.

clue.text: Stops or starts playing billiards

definitions.meaning: ends abruptly, as talks are halted
taking the opening shot in billiards or snooker

explanation.surface: Someone halts or begins a game of billiards.
explanation.definitionFit: To break off is to stop suddenly, and in billiards it is to take the first shot.

clue.text: Knocked flat by a hard bargainer?

definitions.meaning: describes a price forced lower by a tough negotiator

explanation.surface: Someone flattened by a tough negotiator.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten down means flattened by blows, and also describes a price haggled lower.

clue.text: Shrewd fielder in sticky leg trap

parts.note: fly is slang for sharp or knowing
in cricket, a catcher is a fielder who takes catches

explanation.surface: A sharp fielder stands in the leg trap, a ring of close catchers on the batsman's leg side in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket 'leg trap' (close fielders on the leg side) is the misdirection: the trap is a sticky strip that catches insects by the legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flycatcher is a sticky paper trap for flies, which stick to it by their legs.

clue.text: Gamble on race — a chance to win lots of money

definitions.text: a chance to win lots of money

indicators.note: in an across clue one word put on another follows it

parts.note: the (Grand) National is Britain's famous steeplechase horse race
a lottery is a gamble on drawn numbers

explanation.surface: Betting on a horse race gives a shot at a big win.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK's state lottery offers prizes of millions to ticket holders.

clue.text: Completely wrong direction

parts.note: out means mistaken, as in 'your sums are out'
right is a direction

explanation.surface: Someone has gone entirely the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means wholly or completely, as in an outright win.

clue.text: Always includes ten on the outside

indicators.note: one word holding another within it

parts.note: eternal means always lasting
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Something forever counts ten among its exterior parts.
explanation.definitionFit: External means on the outside of something.

clue.text: Cooked best o' fare?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are altered or fiddled

parts.note: taken as written
o' is a clipped 'of', giving O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner names the finest dish on the menu, a cooked one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges BEST O FARE; the whole clue also describes the dish, a traditional British best.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is cooked meat, long held up as the finest of English food.

clue.text: Find love in a home on the water

indicators.note: the letter for love goes within the word for home

parts.note: a flat is a home
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Discover romance in a houseboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Afloat means floating on water.

clue.text: Run a special edition

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run not scored off the bat, such as a wide or bye
an additional newspaper issue printed for late news

explanation.surface: Print a special issue of the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run not off the bat counts as this, and a newspaper's special issue is also one.

clue.text: Follow Rex in to make certain

indicators.note: the king's letter goes inside the word for follow

parts.note: to ensue is to follow on
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Trail the king inside to guarantee something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain something happens.

clue.text: Agreed everything was bound to come out

indicators.note: used here to say one word was enclosed by another

parts.note: tied means bound
all means everything

explanation.surface: Everyone agreed it was inevitable the truth would emerge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to come out' reads as inevitable; 'to come out' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that tallied matched or agreed.

clue.text: Moment that can worry sheep and cattle

definitions.meaning: a brief instant, as in 'wait a second'
a blood-sucking parasite that infests livestock

explanation.surface: A brief time when livestock may be troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is an instant and also a parasitic mite that plagues farm animals.

clue.text: Involving one's stomach in following a strict diet

indicators.note: the answer sits within the following words

explanation.surface: Dieting strictly concerns one's belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric means relating to the stomach.

clue.text: Pluck the strings

definitions.meaning: violin strings were made of catgut

explanation.surface: Pluck the strings of an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Guts means courage, and gut is the traditional material of instrument strings.

clue.text: Jar in which pound may be kept in ready money

indicators.note: one letter is held within the word for money

parts.note: cash is ready money
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A pot where a pound may be stashed in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Jar as a verb means to clash, as colours jar.

clue.text: Treat wage adjustment as a political scandal

indicators.note: an adjustment rearranges, here the letters of the words before it

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Handling a pay change as though it were a government scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Watergate was the 1970s US political scandal that brought down President Nixon.
